# harborpilot_provider (Resource)

An upstream model provider (API, OpenAI-compatible, local, or a CLI bridge) and its models.

Changes made outside Terraform are detected on refresh and shown as a diff of `spec`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "harborpilot_provider" "anthropic" {
  name = "anthropic"
  spec = jsonencode({
    type = "anthropic"
    models = [{
      id                = "claude-sonnet-4-5"
      display_name      = "Claude Sonnet 4.5"
      context_window    = 200000
      max_output_tokens = 64000
      capabilities      = ["tools", "streaming"]
      pricing = {
        currency        = "USD"
        input_per_mtok  = "3"
        output_per_mtok = "15"
        price_version   = "2026-11"
      }
    }]
  })
}

# A local model server (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio) on a private address.
resource "harborpilot_provider" "local" {
  name = "local-vllm"
  spec = jsonencode({
    type                  = "openai_compatible"
    base_url              = "http://10.0.0.5:8000/v1"
    allow_private_network = true
    models                = [{ id = "qwen3-coder", display_name = "Qwen3 Coder", context_window = 131072, max_output_tokens = 16384, capabilities = ["tools", "streaming"] }]
  })
}

# An OpenAI-compatible router: pin a model to one upstream provider and set
# extra request fields (Harbor Pilot 0.1.6 or later). Fields left out of a
# model are cleared on apply.
resource "harborpilot_provider" "router" {
  name = "router"
  spec = jsonencode({
    type         = "openai_compatible"
    display_name = "Router"
    base_url     = "https://router.example.com/v1"
    models = [{
      id = "vendor/model-a"
      provider_routing = {
        only            = ["provider-a"]
        allow_fallbacks = false
        data_collection = "deny"
      }
      request_fields       = { temperature = 0.2, transforms = ["middle-out"] }
      request_field_policy = "configured"
    }]
  })
}
```

## Upstream request fields

Each model in `spec.models` can carry three optional fields. They need Harbor Pilot 0.1.6 or later; an older server rejects them with a 422 validation error (`unexpected property`).

- `provider_routing` pins which upstream provider serves the model. The server sends it as the request body's `provider` object. Its properties are `order`, `only`, `ignore`, `sort` (`price`, `throughput` or `latency`), `allow_fallbacks`, `require_parameters`, `data_collection` (`allow` or `deny`), `zdr`, `quantizations` and `max_price` (`prompt`, `completion`, `request`, `image`). It is accepted only on `openai_compatible` providers.
- `request_fields` is a map of extra upstream request fields. Each value is any JSON value, written as HCL inside `jsonencode`. Numbers are sent exactly as written, so a large integer such as a `seed` keeps every digit.
- `request_field_policy` decides what happens when a client's own request already sets one of these fields: `configured` (the model's value wins, the server's default), `client` (the client's value wins) or `reject` (the request is refused).

**Omitted means cleared.** An apply replaces the whole spec, as the API's `PUT` does. A field you leave out of a model is cleared on the server on the next apply, including values someone set in the Harbor Pilot UI, and an omitted `request_field_policy` reads back as the server's default, `configured`. The provider adds no defaults of its own. To keep a field, write it in `spec`.

**Validation is the server's.** Which `request_fields` names a model may set depends on the provider type: the server keeps an allowlist (sampling, routing between hosts and tagging options) and refuses output limits, tools, stored state, caching and structural fields. The provider doesn't duplicate that list. A refused field fails the apply with the server's 422 message and the field's path, for example:

```
spec.models[0].request_fields.max_tokens: cannot be configured: output limits
bypass the budget reservation and the model's output cap
```

The server stores these fields in a canonical form (for example, with the unset `provider_routing` properties filled in). The provider compares that form with the one from its last apply, so a second plan is empty. A change made outside Terraform shows as a diff of `spec`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`).
- `spec` (String) The provider specification as JSON, usually written with `jsonencode({...})`. See the `ProviderSpec` schema in the Harbor Pilot API reference. Properties you leave out take the server's default, usually their zero value (empty string, list or map, `0`, `false`), except `enabled`, which must be set.

### Read-Only

- `drift_state` (String) `drifted` when the object was changed outside Terraform since Terraform last wrote it.
- `id` (String) Stable object id.
- `managed_by` (String) Source of the last change (`terraform` after an apply).
- `revision` (Number) Server revision, used for optimistic concurrency.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id or by name.
terraform import harborpilot_provider.example <id-or-name>
```
